raw.description:
The Compensation Analyst designs and runs Omilia's sales compensation programme end to end, from plan architecture through to the reporting infrastructure that keeps it accurate every cycle. This role owns both strategy and execution - building compensation plans and SPIFFs from scratch, then running the mechanisms that calculate, track and report on them. Reporting into Revenue Operations, this role partners closely with Sales, Finance and Payroll to keep compensation accurate, timely and aligned to revenue goals.

Accountabilities

  • Own end-to-end design of sales compensation plans and incentive structures aligned to revenue goals.
  • Own the full SPIFF programme lifecycle, from design and launch through payout and ROI retrospective.
  • Own the comp calculation, payout and reporting infrastructure that keeps compensation accurate every cycle.
  • Own compensation plan documentation, quota assignments and plan change history.
  • Own cross-functional alignment with Sales, Finance and Payroll on plan design, quota setting and payout accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

Design and build sales compensation plans and incentive structures aligned to revenue goals.

  • Model plan scenarios and payout economics to test affordability and behavioural impact before rollout.
  • Recommend plan changes based on performance data and market benchmarking.
  • Design, build and launch SPIFF programmes, defining mechanics, eligibility, targets and payout structure.
  • Track SPIFF performance in-flight and report on ROI against target behaviour.
  • Run the end-to-end comp calculation and payout process each cycle.
  • Build and maintain the reporting infrastructure and mechanisms needed to run comp accurately at scale.
  • Build dashboards and reports for comp attainment, plan performance and SPIFF ROI.
  • Partner with Finance on accruals, forecasting and comp cost analysis.
  • Partner with RevOps on the CRM data integrity that feeds every calculation, and flag design issues, payout errors or gaming risk before they escalate.

Requirements

Required:

  • Experience designing and administering sales compensation plans in a B2B SaaS environment.
  • Direct experience building and running SPIFF programmes end to end.
  • Strong Excel and analytical modelling skills.
  • Comfortable owning both the strategic design and the operational mechanics of a compensation programme.
  • High attention to detail, given the direct link to employee pay accuracy.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with comp/ICM platforms (e.g. Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Spiff).
  • Experience running compensation across multiple currencies or regions.
  • Background partnering directly with Finance on comp accruals and forecasting.

Omilia Note

- Contribute actively and effectively as an integrated team member.
- Act as an Omilia ambassador in all interactions.

JOB OBJECTIVE:
The middle market underwriter reviews risks, determines acceptability, and successfully writes profitable business accounts. Within designated authority, reviews insurance applications to evaluate, classify and rate each risk to determine acceptability, coverage and pricing. Responsible for the financial performance of the assigned book of business and is expected to achieve profitable retention and new business growth. Focused on taking action to achieve results that positively impact sales and profitability while ensuring excellent customer service and timely responsiveness to independent agents for their commercial lines accounts.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
1. Determine the acceptability, quality, pricing, profitability and opportunity for new and existing business.
2. Complete thorough risk analysis on designated accounts using appropriate Encova, NCCI, ISO and industry rules, policies, procedures, and guidelines, etc.
3. Identify, create and initiate new business opportunities within current book of business and assigned agencies.
4. Gather and analyze information necessary to make an accurate evaluation of risk.
5. Accept or reject commercial lines accounts that fall outside of straight through processing rules through exposure identification and risk analysis, including:
• understanding all exposures that might cause a policy to incur losses;
• conservatively assessing the likelihood of any exposure actually causing a loss and the probable cost if it does;
• setting a premium that, on average, would deliver a profit after both prospective loss costs and operating expenses are covered;
• be willing to walk away if the appropriate premium cannot be obtained.
6. Apply discretionary pricing appropriately based on risk exposures, risk quality, loss potential, pricing model indications and your letter of authority.
7. Determine acceptability of revision requests that fall outside straight through processing rules and communicate how the revision will be handled to the Associate Underwriter.
8. Communicate all underwriting decisions or changes on coverage, limits, exposures and/or pricing, discussing alternatives with assigned agents as needed.
9. Promote effective agency relationships and encourage continued use of our company products and technology.
10. Provide support to appointed agents by serving as a resource for underwriting questions.
11. Utilizes Encova systems to transact requests and endorsements.
12. Utilize available resources including company underwriting guidelines, business unit strategies, and consultations with others to ensure adequate understanding of risk exposures.
13. Prepare proposals to producers, including negotiation of terms and conditions.
14. Ensure the proper issuance of policies, certificates, filings and notifications.
15. Seek the guidance of management on risks exceeding assigned authority levels.
16. Effectively utilize industry rules and guidance to ensure proper policy construction.
17. Identify underwriting issues; recommend and develop plans for problem resolution and implement them where appropriate.
18. Manage existing and prospective accounts by actively participating in account renewals, new business presentations as needed and discussion with agents.
19. Participate in monitoring and analyzing growth and profitability of assigned agents; initiate actions and understand downstream impact of alternatives.
20. Mentor entry-level underwriters and trainees to achieve profitable retention, growth and customer service standards.
21. Serve as a resource for other team members and units.

OTHER FUNCTIONS:
1. Maintain an awareness of the current objectives and initiatives of Encova Insurance.
2. Maintain an understanding of all products offered by Encova Insurance and be able to guide agents to the appropriate contact for needs outside of commercial lines.
3. Travel to various locations to support business objectives when necessary.

4. Perform other duties as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
• Minimum 2 years of commercial lines underwriting experience in package lines and/or worker’s compensation in the Property and Casualty insurance market strongly preferred.
• Bachelor’s degree preferred, demonstrated significant underwriting experience may substitute.
• Interpersonal skills are required including the ability to demonstrate professionalism, adaptability, accountability, collaboration and problem solving.
• Insurance designations or insurance education course work (i.e. AINS-Associate in General Insurance) strongly preferred.
• Critical thinking: Ability to assess an individual situation and select applicable rules from an array of options, resulting in the most appropriate and sustainable decision.
• Strong oral and written communication skills.
• Knowledge of underwriting laws and rules and their application.
• Knowledge of policy and procedures regarding risk administration and risk management, underwriting and loss control.
• Knowledge of the insurance industry and the business environment in which it operates in order to develop an effective business strategy and remain technically current.
• Thorough understanding of business exposure calculations, classifications, experience rating or other plan modifications.
• Ability to develop and implement account, territorial, producer and book strategies to acquire and retain business.
• Ability to work effectively in a team environment.
• Ability to use logic and reasoning to identify strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems.
• Ability to identify complex problems and review related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.
• Ability to make sound decisions after considering all facts, potential risks, customer needs and alternative solutions.
• Ability to initiate and build relationships and tailor services to meet customer needs.
• Ability to present ideas and information to individuals and groups in a clear, concise, influential, organized and diplomatic manner and address concerns or needs.
• Ability to adjust priorities based on changing situations.
• Ability to effectively manage multiple assignments while meeting established guidelines.

• Proficient in Excel.

This position has been evaluated in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Encova Insurance makes every effort to reasonably accommodate disabilities to permit performance of the essential functions and candidates who need such accommodation are encouraged to seek it. This description reflects the nature and level of work performed by associates in this position. It is not an all-inclusive inventory of duties, responsibilities and qualifications required. It provides an accurate overview of the work and skills needed to perform this position. Because job content may change from time to time, Encova Insurance reserves the right to add and/or delete functions from this job as it deems necessary for business reasons.

At Encova Insurance, we firmly believe that our associates drive our company's success by delivering unrivaled service to our customers. raw.description:
Role Summary

The Chief Legal Officer (CLO) is the senior legal executive responsible for overseeing the organization's legal strategy, governance, regulatory compliance, corporate affairs, and risk management. The CLO serves as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and executive leadership team, ensuring the organization operates within legal and regulatory frameworks while supporting business growth and strategic initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

1. Legal Strategy & Executive Advisory

  • Serve as the principal legal advisor to the CEO, Board, and executive leadership team.
  • Develop and execute the organization's legal strategy in alignment with business objectives.
  • Provide legal guidance on strategic initiatives, mergers and acquisitions, partnerships, and corporate restructuring.
  • Anticipate and mitigate legal risks associated with business operations and growth.

2. Corporate Governance

  • Ensure compliance with corporate governance standards and best practices.
  • Advise the Board and executive leadership on fiduciary responsibilities and governance matters.
  • Manage board resolutions, corporate records, and governance policies.
  • Support corporate secretarial functions where applicable.

3. Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management

  • Oversee enterprise-wide legal and regulatory compliance programs.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards.
  • Monitor regulatory developments and assess their impact on the organization.
  • Develop legal risk mitigation frameworks and compliance controls.

4. Contracts & Commercial Transactions

  • Lead the negotiation, drafting, and review of significant commercial agreements.
  • Oversee contract management processes and legal documentation standards.
  • Provide legal support for strategic partnerships, vendor agreements, and customer contracts.
  • Ensure contractual arrangements adequately protect organizational interests.

5. Litigation & Dispute Resolution

  • Manage litigation strategy and external legal counsel relationships.
  • Oversee dispute resolution, arbitration, mediation, and regulatory investigations.
  • Assess litigation exposure and recommend appropriate legal actions.
  • Ensure effective management of legal claims and liabilities.

6. Mergers, Acquisitions & Corporate Transactions

  • Lead legal due diligence for mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, and investments.
  • Structure transactions to minimize legal and regulatory risk.
  • Manage external advisors and legal workstreams throughout transaction lifecycles.
  • Support post-merger integration activities from a legal perspective.

7. Ethics, Compliance & Corporate Integrity

  • Promote a culture of ethics, integrity, and compliance.
  • Oversee whistleblower programs, investigations, and ethics policies.
  • Ensure adherence to anti-corruption, anti-bribery, and corporate conduct standards.
  • Lead internal investigations involving legal and compliance matters.

8. Legal Team Leadership

  • Build and lead a high-performing legal and compliance function.
  • Manage legal budgets and external counsel expenditures.
  • Develop legal talent and succession planning initiatives.
  • Establish legal operations processes and performance metrics.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Juris Doctor (JD), LLB, or equivalent law degree.
  • Licensed attorney admitted to practice in a relevant jurisdiction.
  • 15+ years of progressive legal experience.
  • Minimum 5+ years in a senior legal leadership role (General Counsel, CLO, Head of Legal, Legal Director).
  • Experience advising executive leadership and boards of directors.
  • Strong background in corporate law, governance, compliance, commercial contracts, and regulatory matters.
  • Experience managing complex legal transactions and litigation.

After-Hours Travel Consultant

A world where tech and people work collectively to make corporate travel simpler, faster and easier.

Corporate Traveler is one of Flight Centre Travel Group’s (FCTG) most successful brands, globally. Our mission is to dominate the SME market, making the end-to-end travel experience faster, simpler and easier for our customers and to demonstrate ongoing value to decision-makers, travelers and bookers. We provide our customers with the perfect blend of personal, local service blended with our expert technology suite and the great choice and value which comes with being part of the FCTG family. For decades, we’ve been helping go-getter businesses grow through travel.

Corporate Traveler has offices across a global network that spans Australia, Canada, USA, UK, South Africa and New Zealand. The brand has been part of the Flight Centre Travel Group for more than 26 years and is a key contributor to the ongoing strength of FCTG’s corporate travel division. Award winning, forward thinking and fun to work for – this is a business for people who love travel, are team players and customer service oriented.

To learn more about Corporate Traveler please click HERE

About The Opportunity

As part of the After Hours Support Team, you help deliver exceptional travel management services for Stage and Screen clients during non-business hours when day teams are unavailable. You provide direct, hands-on support to production crews, touring artists, athletic teams, entertainment executives, and sports professionals, managing urgent travel needs and critical travel disruptions common in the fast-paced entertainment and sports industries.

Working within a fully remote team, you handle client interactions via phone and email with professionalism, speed, and care, escalating operational questions to the Leader on Shift (LOS) as needed. Your contributions ensure the client experience maintains Corporate Traveler's high standards of service excellence, adapting to the unique demands of entertainment productions, touring schedules, and sporting events.

Key Responsibilities

  • Ensure a high level of client satisfaction with their Corporate Traveler after-hours experience by exceeding customer service expectations via phone and email.
  • Utilize Sabre GDS and various booking platforms including NDC and web-based programs to arrange accurate business travel reservations, including air, car, hotel, and ground transportation.
  • Respond to urgent travel needs, production delays, event changes, and last-minute itinerary modifications for Stage and Screen clients.
  • Follow company procedures, account guidelines, and customer service standards.
  • Escalate complex issues, disruptions, or high-value client situations to the Leader on Shift (LOS) as appropriate.
  • Work as a team member, assisting other agents as needed to complete all functions related to servicing the client.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with clients and colleagues.
  • Develop working knowledge of entertainment and sports travel requirements, including group movements, tour logistics, and event-driven schedules.
  • Other duties and tasks as assigned
  • Contribute to a safe, inclusive, and accessible work environment where all Flighties feel welcomed, respected, and supported to thrive

Experience & Qualifications

  • Experience with a GDS system, Sabre preferred.
  • Customer-focused, consistently going above and beyond to deliver an amazing client experience.
  • Outstanding interpersonal skills and ability to build strong business relationships.
  • A problem solver who thinks outside the box to provide creative solutions.
  • High attention to detail with the ability to effectively multi-task and shift gears in time-sensitive situations.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Positive attitude with a hunger for knowledge, able to work well under pressure and adapt to change.
  • Tech savvy and comfortable learning new software.
  • Reliable, high-speed internet connectivity required to support core job responsibilities, including but not limited to video conferencing, access to company systems, and secure handling of company data.

A typical schedule will include a 40-hour work week with various shifts including weekends, overnights, and holidays—flexibility is a MUST.

Work Perks! - What’s in it for you:

FCTG is renowned internationally for having amazing perks and an even better culture. We understand that our people are our most valuable asset. It is the passion and dedication of our teams that keep the company on top of the industry ladder. It’s also why we offer some great employee benefits and perks outside of the norm.

  • Have fun:At the heart of everything we do at Flight Centre is a desire to have fun.
  • Reward & Recognition: Celebrate the success of yourself and others at our regular Buzz Nights and at the annual Global Gathering - You'll have to experience it to believe it!
  • Use your smarts:Our people use their quick thinking, expertise, and tenacity to always figure things out.
  • Love for travel:We were founded by people who wanted to travel and want others to do the same. That passion is something you can’t miss in our people or service.
  • Personal connections:We are a big business founded on personal relationships.
  • Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion through initiatives like Diversity Day (paid leave to observe a holiday or cultural celebration of your choice) Employee Resource Groups (Racial Equity, Gender Equity, LGBTQ2IA+, Accessibility, Environmental Justice), DEI education initiatives, and equitable practices, including regular equity assessments and inclusive recruitment protocols.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

About Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and family, be your true self and live a full life. You will have access to:

  • Career development with an international company where you can grow the career you dream of.
  • A company recognized as a great place to work in dozens of countries around the world and named one of the most admired companies in the world by Fortune.
  • A company that is recognized as one of the best big companies to work for as well as a best place to work for diversity, working mothers, female executives, and scientists.

The Opportunity

This is an 18-month contract position and works remotely in the Abbott Diabetes Care covering Western Ontario and Manitoba through Alberta. We’re focused on helping people with diabetes manage their health with life-changing products that provide accurate data to drive better-informed decisions. We’re revolutionizing the way people monitor their glucose levels with our new sensing technology.

The Medical Science Liaison (MSL) is the medical / scientific voice of expertise for Abbott Diabetes Care (ADC) products and therapeutic areas. This field-based role focuses on scientific engagement with ADC stakeholders. Provides scientific expert advice / guidance to key customers for ADC products & relevant therapeutic areas, including scientific exchange & professional development with key thought leaders / external experts and provides medical / scientific affairs support to the Canadian commercial team. The MSL serves to support the scientific credibility of ADC with established and emerging national & regional thoughts leaders, by supporting scientific dialogue and collaboration in areas of research, scientific publications, and scientific exchange, including unsolicited requests for medical information. They also interface regularly with appropriate Canadian commercial team members. They maintain a high level of knowledge to ensure credible dissemination of scientific information and dialogue with thoughts leaders, healthcare providers and healthcare organizations.

What You’ll Do

  • The Primary focus of the MSL will be to establish, foster and maintain relationships with key opinion leaders to build outstanding scientific data awareness and advocacy in the field.
  • Ensure a strong medical and scientific presence for ADC in key academic centers by facilitation of research initiatives.
  • Create and execute a short and long-term clinical, scientific support plan based on understanding unmet needs of the key opinion leaders and the competitive landscape.
  • Work collaboratively and cross-functionally with other in-field members (Continuing Health Education, Market Access, Sales) while retaining functional independence.
  • The MSL will provide clinical protocol expertise to investigators for use in company sponsored and ensure that they are consistent with the company’s objectives, HC regulations, and necessary approvals.
  • Provide support to investigators about the process and areas of interest regarding the Investigator Initiated Study program
  • The MSL will act as a clinical and scientific resource within the Medical Affairs organization for information pertaining to disease states and the company’s products to ensure awareness and understanding.
  • Deliver credible presentations on scientific matters to health care providers, individually or in groups (meetings, clinical sessions, etc.), where requested.
  • Participate in the selection process to identify appropriately qualified thought leaders, ADC would wish to engage in collaborative efforts – such as educational and advisory roles (Advisory Boards, Congresses, Symposia, etc.) while ensuring a high level of scientific integrity in these collaborative efforts.
  • Attend relevant scientific meetings and conferences. Collaborate with internal stakeholders to develop summaries of key data and other scientifically relevant information to inform ADC strategic priorities and initiatives. Staff the Medical Affairs area of the exhibit booth at national scientific meetings and congresses
  • Provide key thought leaders / external experts with scientific and technical support for publications of scientific or medical interest.
  • Ensure that all activities and interactions are conducted with due regard to all applicable local and national laws, regulations, guidelines, codes of conduct, company policies and accepted standards of best practice.

Required Qualifications

  • Medical or Scientific degree (NP, M.D., PhD or Pharm D.) is preferred but candidates with a degree in a relevant discipline or CDE and demonstrated experience will be considered.
  • Minimum 1 year of experience in an MSL role in the pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical/device industry/health care.
  • Must be able to travel 50% of the time, including ability to travel overnight and occasionally on weekends.
  • Proven ability to work independently with excellent self-leadership.
  • Demonstrates ability to function with minimal supervision and a high degree of initiative.
  • Demonstrates in depth scientific and clinical knowledge and ability to understand and integrate complex scientific concepts.
  • Possess superior communication skills (written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills).
  • Strong negotiation skills and ability to build partnerships with opinion leaders.
  • Understanding of Clinical Research/Good Clinical Practice.
  • Diabetes experience is preferred.

raw.description:
About BTA Design Services

Headquartered in Ottawa, BTA Design Services supports the electronic design community across Canada and internationally, specializing in ASIC and FPGA design, verification, and embedded software development. We strengthen our clients' engineering teams and accelerate the delivery of complete, production ready designs.

We are adaptable, efficient, and built around exceptional technical talent. Our continued growth reflects the trust our clients place in us, and we are currently searching globally for a Senior Physical Design Engineer with deep expertise in place and route.

About the Engagement

You will join BTA Design Services as an employee and work on behalf of one of our clients, an industry leader building advanced silicon platforms for next generation AI infrastructure. The work pairs leading edge CMOS design with the bandwidth and power demands of modern AI, and the client partners with the world's foremost foundries to bring frontier designs to production. Further details are shared with candidates under confidentiality during the interview process.

This engagement places you at the center of that work, delivering world-class ASICs on the most demanding technology nodes in the industry.

About the Position

As a Senior Physical Design Engineer, you will own backend implementation from netlist to GDSII on challenging blocks and sub-systems. You will apply advanced flows and techniques on single-digit FinFET technology nodes, working alongside a strong and experienced team to bring complex designs to closure. This is a senior, fully remote role, and you may be located anywhere.

Key Responsibilities

  • Run place and route implementation flows and analyze the results.
  • Create effective floorplans that support physically aware synthesis.
  • Drive designs to timing closure and run physical verification.
  • Debug issues spanning tools, timing constraints, DFT, and design.
  • Partner with the design team to improve RTL and make it implementation friendly.
  • Implement and apply timing ECOs.
  • Run PrimeTime and analyze timing reports.
  • Develop strategies to optimize power and area.
  • Run IR-drop analysis and identify optimal strategies to improve it.
  • Interface with analog and front-end teams to align on shared objectives.

Key Qualifications

  • 8 or more years of relevant experience in ASIC digital place and route.
  • Recent, hands-on experience with leading EDA tools and advanced flows (Synopsys and Cadence).
  • Strong understanding of advanced FinFET technology nodes, DRC rules, and node-specific P&R requirements.
  • Practical experience with floorplanning.
  • Solid grasp of CTS concepts and the ability to design clocks to meet timing requirements.
  • Working knowledge of IR-drop optimization strategies.
  • Experience with timing closure and ECO implementation (PT-ECO or Tweaker experience is an asset).
  • Strong scripting skills.
  • Exposure to several of the following: synthesis, StarRC, PT DMSA, RedHawk, Calibre, and formal verification (LEC or Formality).
  • A track record as a self-starter who also works well within a team.

Remote Work

This role is fully remote and open to candidates in any location. You will collaborate with distributed engineering teams across time zones, so strong written communication, self-direction, and the discipline to deliver independently are essential.

Why Work With Us

We offer challenging, stimulating technical work with companies that lead the world in technology and innovation. At BTA Design Services, we know our strength lies in the people who join us, so we foster an environment where everyone is trusted, valued, and engaged. We also believe work-life balance matters, and we give our engineers demanding, rewarding roles while leaving room for family, friends, and life beyond work.
This is a new position. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

SEI's Wealth business is seeking a results-oriented Practice Management Consultant to specialize in helping advisory firms gain and maintain scale—capacity, efficiency, and consistency—through their people and culture.

This people-centric leader will be responsible for helping to build and evolve SEI's Practice Management "scale" function in close partnership with SEI’s Technology and Operations Consultant and alongside the "growth" and "evolve" functions. An ideal candidate is willing and able to strategize, experiment, and execute solutions that deliver actionable and impactful advice and resources to SEI’s independent broker dealer and RIA clients. We're looking for an individual who is an expert in all things talent—hiring, onboarding, management, leadership, culture, talent development, and compensation planning—helping firms build and develop high-performing teams that drive sustainable growth, profitability, and enterprise value.

This role will also help advisory firms evolve their talent strategy to evolve in an everchanging, digital and AI-native world—reimagining roles, workflows, competencies, and career paths as AI and automation reshape how advisory work gets done. The consultant will guide firms in identifying which capabilities to build internally, which to augment with technology, and how to prepare their teams to thrive alongside AI-enabled tools and platforms.

Equally important, this consultant will help advisors think like business owners when it comes to their people—treating talent and productivity as strategic investments rather than operational expenses. They will coach firm leaders on measuring return on talent, aligning compensation and productivity, making disciplined hiring and workforce planning decisions, and building the systems, metrics, and management practices that turn a group of professionals into a scalable, high-performing enterprise.

This practice management role is tailored for individuals deeply enthusiastic about the independent advisor profession, committed to ongoing learning, and able to leverage their expertise in talent, people, and culture to drive meaningful outcomes within advisory practices. An ideal candidate possesses a background as a Chief People Officer, Head of Talent, HR leader, COO, business owner, coach, or consultant with substantial real-world experience helping service businesses build and scale high-performing teams, and is experienced and networked in the wealth management industry. They understand the unique talent challenges of independent advisory firms of all sizes—both small ($100M+) and large firms ($2B+ AUM)—and are excited to expand our practice management advice and resources to support scalable growth through people.

This role is a remote role. The role requires up to 20% travel.

What you will do:

  • Coach advisors to think like business owners when it comes to their people—treating talent and productivity as strategic investments, measuring return on talent, and applying disciplined workforce planning, capacity, and compensation decisions to drive profitability and enterprise value.

  • Conduct thorough assessments of firms' talent, leadership, organizational, and cultural strengths, gaps, and readiness, and offer actionable and customized recommendations.

  • Develop and deliver engaging content including presentations, workshops, and training sessions to advisors and their teams on talent, people, culture, and related practice management topics.

  • Create scalable resources, tools, playbooks, frameworks, and educational content to help advisors plan for and execute team-building, leadership succession, and culture development as they grow organically and inorganically.

  • Build and deliver curriculum designed to develop the next generation of advisors, operations leads, and firm leaders—supporting career pathing, competency building, and long-term firm sustainability.

  • Lead and grow the SEI Next Gen Community, creating meaningful development experiences, peer networking opportunities, and ongoing educational programming for emerging advisor and operations talent.

  • Partner closely with SEI's People and Culture team to bring proven talent best practices to SEI's advisor clients, including StrengthsFinder, DISC, and other behavioral assessments, leadership development tools, and organizational effectiveness frameworks.

  • Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to advance how SEI connects talent with hiring advisory firms at scale.

  • Work in close partnership with fellow Practice Management Consultants across the growth, scale, and transition pillars to deliver holistic, integrated advice to advisors.

  • Build and manage strategic partnerships with external talent-focused experts, consultants, coaches, assessment providers, and service providers to deliver additional value to advisors.

  • Direct and manage special projects on the Advisor Services Team related to talent, workforce development, and culture-focused strategies.

  • Act as a thought leader by contributing articles, webinars, podcasts, and other educational content on talent, leadership, and culture within advisory firms.

What we need from you:

  • A minimum of 7 years of experience helping financial advisors and/or professional service firms grow, scale, and strengthen their businesses through roles in talent management, human resources, organizational development, coaching, consulting, practice management, or leadership within advisory firms.

  • Deep expertise across the full employee lifecycle, including workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, performance management, leadership development, compensation design, succession planning, engagement, and retention.

  • Working knowledge of how AI, automation, and digital tools are reshaping roles, workflows, and productivity within professional service and advisory firms—and how to translate that into practical talent strategy.

  • Business-owner mindset with the ability to help firm leaders view talent and productivity as strategic investments—measuring ROI, aligning compensation with outcomes, and connecting people decisions to enterprise value.

  • First-hand experience building, leading, and developing high-performing teams—ideally within advisory firms or similar professional service businesses.

  • Deep understanding of the independent advisor and RIA landscape, including the unique talent, leadership, and culture challenges facing advisory firms today.

  • Experience designing and facilitating leadership development programs, team workshops, and educational experiences for professionals at all career stages.

  • Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with an ability to present complex topics in a clear, confident, and compelling way.

  • Experience in multi-channel communication mediums, including individual face-to-face interactions, in-person and virtual one-to-many presentations, live video, recorded video, phone and email.

  • Passion for developing others, particularly next-generation advisor and operations talent.

Responsible for all aspects of strategizing and executing programmatic and awareness media campaigns across a variety of platforms and through direct media partnerships for clients. You use your expertise to drive growth through initial planning, execution, monitoring, optimization, analysis, and reporting.

Beyond DSP activation, you understand how to execute high-impact campaigns across the broader awareness media landscape through direct partnerships, including endemic media, CTV, linear TV, Out of Home (OOH), and print.

This role will serve as the day-to-day subject matter expert (SME) for programmatic and awareness media for our clients, providing strategic recommendations, media planning, analysis, and reporting while responding to ad-hoc requests. You will be responsible for developing sophisticated media strategies, identifying the right channels and partners to reach target audiences, and delivering outstanding communication, service, and campaign performance for our clients.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the clients’ go-to expert in Programmatic and Awareness Media while overseeing the broader media strategy and performance of client campaigns
  • Own end-to-end campaign strategy and execution across programmatic platforms, with a strong emphasis on The Trade Desk, as well as direct media partnerships
  • Develop and execute integrated media strategies across programmatic, endemic, CTV, linear TV, OOH, print, and other awareness channels
  • Establish and manage direct publisher and media partnerships, including negotiations, media planning, activation, and reporting
  • Build and present multi-channel media plans with clear budget allocations, KPIs, pacing, and testing roadmaps
  • Drive continuous optimization using a deep understanding of real-time bidding, audience segmentation, platform algorithms, and broader media performance
  • Collaborate with creative and analytics teams to develop test-and-learn strategies that improve campaign effectiveness across channels
  • Provide high-touch communication with clients, including strategic recommendations, performance reporting, and actionable next steps
  • Stay ahead of trends across ad tech, emerging media opportunities, platform capabilities, and data privacy regulations to inform and future-proof campaign strategy
  • Analyze performance across channels, synthesize insights, and deliver executive-level reporting and recommendations
  • Develop strategic roadmaps and test plans that ladder up to client business goals with a strong focus on efficiency, scale, and brand impact
  • Train and mentor junior team members in programmatic and broader media planning and activation best practices

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in paid media with deep, hands-on expertise in Programmatic advertising
  • Strong proficiency in at least one major DSP, including The Trade Desk, DV360, or Amazon DSP; experience with The Trade Desk is highly preferred
  • Experience establishing and managing direct media partnerships across endemic, CTV, linear TV, OOH, and/or print to support broader awareness media strategies
  • Demonstrated experience with publisher negotiations, media planning and strategy, campaign activation, and reporting
  • Experience developing sophisticated, multi-channel media strategies across both programmatic and direct media buys
  • Skilled in media analytics, forecasting, pacing, testing, and translating insights into actionable recommendations
  • Comfortable managing multi-million-dollar media budgets with accountability to campaign KPIs and broader business objectives
  • Excellent communication and client-facing skills, with the ability to simplify complex media strategies and drive alignment
  • Strong understanding of attribution, measurement, audience strategy, and incrementality testing
  • Self-starter mindset with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, and collaborative environment

raw.description:
The Compensation Analyst designs and runs Omilia's sales compensation programme end to end, from plan architecture through to the reporting infrastructure that keeps it accurate every cycle. This role owns both strategy and execution - building compensation plans and SPIFFs from scratch, then running the mechanisms that calculate, track and report on them. Reporting into Revenue Operations, this role partners closely with Sales, Finance and Payroll to keep compensation accurate, timely and aligned to revenue goals.

Accountabilities

  • Own end-to-end design of sales compensation plans and incentive structures aligned to revenue goals.
  • Own the full SPIFF programme lifecycle, from design and launch through payout and ROI retrospective.
  • Own the comp calculation, payout and reporting infrastructure that keeps compensation accurate every cycle.
  • Own compensation plan documentation, quota assignments and plan change history.
  • Own cross-functional alignment with Sales, Finance and Payroll on plan design, quota setting and payout accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

Design and build sales compensation plans and incentive structures aligned to revenue goals.

  • Model plan scenarios and payout economics to test affordability and behavioural impact before rollout.
  • Recommend plan changes based on performance data and market benchmarking.
  • Design, build and launch SPIFF programmes, defining mechanics, eligibility, targets and payout structure.
  • Track SPIFF performance in-flight and report on ROI against target behaviour.
  • Run the end-to-end comp calculation and payout process each cycle.
  • Build and maintain the reporting infrastructure and mechanisms needed to run comp accurately at scale.
  • Build dashboards and reports for comp attainment, plan performance and SPIFF ROI.
  • Partner with Finance on accruals, forecasting and comp cost analysis.
  • Partner with RevOps on the CRM data integrity that feeds every calculation, and flag design issues, payout errors or gaming risk before they escalate.

Requirements

Required:

  • Experience designing and administering sales compensation plans in a B2B SaaS environment.
  • Direct experience building and running SPIFF programmes end to end.
  • Strong Excel and analytical modelling skills.
  • Comfortable owning both the strategic design and the operational mechanics of a compensation programme.
  • High attention to detail, given the direct link to employee pay accuracy.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with comp/ICM platforms (e.g. Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Spiff).
  • Experience running compensation across multiple currencies or regions.
  • Background partnering directly with Finance on comp accruals and forecasting.

Omilia Note

- Contribute actively and effectively as an integrated team member.
- Act as an Omilia ambassador in all interactions.

This role will report to a Regional Vice President, Commercial Lines.

Are you a Referral?

If you know a current Encova Insurance associate and would like to apply as a referral, please encourage them to submit your referral information before you submit your application. You will receive an email with a direct URL link to the Job Posting of interest. Applying through this URL link will create your referral relationship for our Talent Acquisition Team.

Encova is only able to employ associates who reside and work within specific U.S. states. Our current policies are based on the laws in states in which we are registered for payroll. Our current footprint includes:

Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin.

JOB OBJECTIVE:
The middle market underwriter reviews risks, determines acceptability, and successfully writes profitable business accounts. Within designated authority, reviews insurance applications to evaluate, classify and rate each risk to determine acceptability, coverage and pricing. Responsible for the financial performance of the assigned book of business and is expected to achieve profitable retention and new business growth. Focused on taking action to achieve results that positively impact sales and profitability while ensuring excellent customer service and timely responsiveness to independent agents for their commercial lines accounts.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
1. Determine the acceptability, quality, pricing, profitability and opportunity for new and existing business.
2. Complete thorough risk analysis on designated accounts using appropriate Encova, NCCI, ISO and industry rules, policies, procedures, and guidelines, etc.
3. Identify, create and initiate new business opportunities within current book of business and assigned agencies.
4. Gather and analyze information necessary to make an accurate evaluation of risk.
5. Accept or reject commercial lines accounts that fall outside of straight through processing rules through exposure identification and risk analysis, including:
• understanding all exposures that might cause a policy to incur losses;
• conservatively assessing the likelihood of any exposure actually causing a loss and the probable cost if it does;
• setting a premium that, on average, would deliver a profit after both prospective loss costs and operating expenses are covered;
• be willing to walk away if the appropriate premium cannot be obtained.
6. Apply discretionary pricing appropriately based on risk exposures, risk quality, loss potential, pricing model indications and your letter of authority.
7. Determine acceptability of revision requests that fall outside straight through processing rules and communicate how the revision will be handled to the Associate Underwriter.
8. Communicate all underwriting decisions or changes on coverage, limits, exposures and/or pricing, discussing alternatives with assigned agents as needed.
9. Promote effective agency relationships and encourage continued use of our company products and technology.
10. Provide support to appointed agents by serving as a resource for underwriting questions.
11. Utilizes Encova systems to transact requests and endorsements.
12. Utilize available resources including company underwriting guidelines, business unit strategies, and consultations with others to ensure adequate understanding of risk exposures.
13. Prepare proposals to producers, including negotiation of terms and conditions.
14. Ensure the proper issuance of policies, certificates, filings and notifications.
15. Seek the guidance of management on risks exceeding assigned authority levels.
16. Effectively utilize industry rules and guidance to ensure proper policy construction.
17. Identify underwriting issues; recommend and develop plans for problem resolution and implement them where appropriate.
18. Manage existing and prospective accounts by actively participating in account renewals, new business presentations as needed and discussion with agents.
19. Participate in monitoring and analyzing growth and profitability of assigned agents; initiate actions and understand downstream impact of alternatives.
20. Mentor entry-level underwriters and trainees to achieve profitable retention, growth and customer service standards.
21. Serve as a resource for other team members and units.

OTHER FUNCTIONS:
1. Maintain an awareness of the current objectives and initiatives of Encova Insurance.
2. Maintain an understanding of all products offered by Encova Insurance and be able to guide agents to the appropriate contact for needs outside of commercial lines.
3. Travel to various locations to support business objectives when necessary.

4. Perform other duties as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
• Minimum 2 years of commercial lines underwriting experience in package lines and/or worker’s compensation in the Property and Casualty insurance market strongly preferred.
• Bachelor’s degree preferred, demonstrated significant underwriting experience may substitute.
• Interpersonal skills are required including the ability to demonstrate professionalism, adaptability, accountability, collaboration and problem solving.
• Insurance designations or insurance education course work (i.e. AINS-Associate in General Insurance) strongly preferred.
• Critical thinking: Ability to assess an individual situation and select applicable rules from an array of options, resulting in the most appropriate and sustainable decision.
• Strong oral and written communication skills.
• Knowledge of underwriting laws and rules and their application.
• Knowledge of policy and procedures regarding risk administration and risk management, underwriting and loss control.
• Knowledge of the insurance industry and the business environment in which it operates in order to develop an effective business strategy and remain technically current.
• Thorough understanding of business exposure calculations, classifications, experience rating or other plan modifications.
• Ability to develop and implement account, territorial, producer and book strategies to acquire and retain business.
• Ability to work effectively in a team environment.
• Ability to use logic and reasoning to identify strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems.

Role Summary

The Chief Legal Officer (CLO) is the senior legal executive responsible for overseeing the organization's legal strategy, governance, regulatory compliance, corporate affairs, and risk management. The CLO serves as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and executive leadership team, ensuring the organization operates within legal and regulatory frameworks while supporting business growth and strategic initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

1. Legal Strategy & Executive Advisory

  • Serve as the principal legal advisor to the CEO, Board, and executive leadership team.
  • Develop and execute the organization's legal strategy in alignment with business objectives.
  • Provide legal guidance on strategic initiatives, mergers and acquisitions, partnerships, and corporate restructuring.
  • Anticipate and mitigate legal risks associated with business operations and growth.

2. Corporate Governance

  • Ensure compliance with corporate governance standards and best practices.
  • Advise the Board and executive leadership on fiduciary responsibilities and governance matters.
  • Manage board resolutions, corporate records, and governance policies.
  • Support corporate secretarial functions where applicable.

3. Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management

  • Oversee enterprise-wide legal and regulatory compliance programs.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards.
  • Monitor regulatory developments and assess their impact on the organization.
  • Develop legal risk mitigation frameworks and compliance controls.

4. Contracts & Commercial Transactions

  • Lead the negotiation, drafting, and review of significant commercial agreements.
  • Oversee contract management processes and legal documentation standards.
  • Provide legal support for strategic partnerships, vendor agreements, and customer contracts.
  • Ensure contractual arrangements adequately protect organizational interests.

5. Litigation & Dispute Resolution

  • Manage litigation strategy and external legal counsel relationships.
  • Oversee dispute resolution, arbitration, mediation, and regulatory investigations.
  • Assess litigation exposure and recommend appropriate legal actions.
  • Ensure effective management of legal claims and liabilities.

6. Mergers, Acquisitions & Corporate Transactions

  • Lead legal due diligence for mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, and investments.
  • Structure transactions to minimize legal and regulatory risk.
  • Manage external advisors and legal workstreams throughout transaction lifecycles.
  • Support post-merger integration activities from a legal perspective.

7. Ethics, Compliance & Corporate Integrity

  • Promote a culture of ethics, integrity, and compliance.
  • Oversee whistleblower programs, investigations, and ethics policies.
  • Ensure adherence to anti-corruption, anti-bribery, and corporate conduct standards.
  • Lead internal investigations involving legal and compliance matters.

8. Legal Team Leadership

  • Build and lead a high-performing legal and compliance function.
  • Manage legal budgets and external counsel expenditures.
  • Develop legal talent and succession planning initiatives.
  • Establish legal operations processes and performance metrics.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Juris Doctor (JD), LLB, or equivalent law degree.
  • Licensed attorney admitted to practice in a relevant jurisdiction.
  • 15+ years of progressive legal experience.
  • Minimum 5+ years in a senior legal leadership role (General Counsel, CLO, Head of Legal, Legal Director).
  • Experience advising executive leadership and boards of directors.
  • Strong background in corporate law, governance, compliance, commercial contracts, and regulatory matters.
  • Experience managing complex legal transactions and litigation.

About Landing

We are a nationwide hospitality platform where fully-furnished apartments meet hotel quality and consistency. Guests access a curated selection of thousands of high-quality apartments available for any length of stay in hundreds of cities nationwide.

By blending the best of hospitality and everyday comfort, every unit is designed with all the amenities of home backed by 24/7 local support. For a week-long getaway or an extended adventure, We deliver a familiar and frictionless guest experience that’s perfect for any travel occasion, for work or pleasure.

For property owners, We offer a fast path to new revenue and higher occupancy in just weeks by tapping into our nationwide demand for furnished, hospitality-grade housing. We provide a turnkey solution that covers the entire unit experience, from furnishings to guest turnover and everything in between, with zero operational lift from partners. We handle it all so partners can unlock value faster.

The Role

We’re looking for a highly analytical and strategic pricing leader to own revenue optimization across our rapidly growing portfolio. This role sits at the intersection of data science, strategy, and execution, responsible for driving measurable impact on occupancy, revenue, and profitability.

You’ll partner closely with Marketing, Product, Engineering, and Operations to shape pricing decisions at the home, market, and network level.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own pricing and revenue optimization strategy for all homes, balancing occupancy, rate, and contribution profit.
  • Enhance and scale our machine learning–driven pricing model.
  • Develop and deploy dynamic pricing logic for lifecycle stages (launch vs. mature), stay lengths, and distribution channels.
  • Build and maintain pricing and performance dashboards using Python, SQL, and Looker.
  • Run elasticity tests, scenario modeling, and pacing analysis to guide decisions with a test-and-learn mindset.
  • Integrate external data sources (AirDNA, CoStar) into pricing strategies.
  • Partner with Marketing on channel mix and ROAS tradeoffs, ensuring OTA vs. direct pricing alignment.
  • Present insights and recommendations to senior leadership to influence revenue and investment decisions.

What You’ll Bring

  • 7–10+ years of experience in pricing, revenue management, or data analytics (ideally in hospitality, travel, or other perishable-inventory industries).
  • Hands-on fluency with revenue management systems and multi-property pricing strategies.
  • Experience building or managing algorithmic or ML-based pricing systems.
  • Deep understanding of price elasticity, occupancy forecasting, and RevPAR optimization.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to distill complex analyses for executives.
  • High bias for action and comfort operating in a fast-paced, data-driven environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with OTA pricing or channel management (Airbnb, Expedia, Booking.com).
  • Familiarity with CoStar or AirDNA datasets.
  • Strong Python skills (pandas, statsmodels, etc.) for building revenue analytics and modeling.
  • Ability to design and interpret statistical tests to balance revenue and conversion outcomes.
  • Experience in high-growth startups or tech-enabled real estate.

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation + stock options
  • Comprehensive benefits — Medical, Dental, Vision, Life and AD&D, Disability, Mental Health, Pet, Commuter, FSA or HSA
  • 401(k) plan and access to ImmediatePay
  • Generous PTO policy
  • Opportunities for upward mobility — we want you to grow with us
  • $750 annually in Landing Stays

Landing is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, including pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, and related conditions, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service or obligation, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

About CoinPoker

Welcome to CoinPoker, the innovative crypto-poker platform where advanced blockchain technology meets the thrilling world of online poker. At CoinPoker, we are revolutionizing the poker experience by offering fast, secure, and transparent gameplay. With recent substantial investment, we are poised to take over the online crypto-poker space and are expanding our team to support our growth.

The Opportunity

The Customer Support Representative is the first point of contact for players on our crypto poker platform, responsible for delivering fast, accurate, and friendly assistance via email. The role covers the full player journey, from onboarding and account queries to gameplay issues, crypto deposits/withdrawals, and responsible gambling support, while protecting platform integrity by identifying fraud, bonus abuse, or suspicious transaction activity. Given the 24/7, real-money nature of a crypto poker product, the representative must operate with strong judgement under time pressure, follow strict escalation protocols, and build genuine trust with a global, crypto-literate player base.

We are looking for two additions to the team to work the afternoon UTC shift (range 14:00 to 00:00).This schedule for this role will include weekend work.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Respond to player inquiries via live chat and/or email in a timely, professional, and on-brand manner, covering account, gameplay, bonus, and technical questions.

  • Assist players with crypto deposits, withdrawals, wallet issues, and transaction status checks, escalating disputed or delayed transactions per SOP.

  • Explain platform terms clearly - wagering requirements, bonus rules, poker-specific rules (rake, tournament structures, table rules), and account limits.

  • Monitor player activity for signs of fraud, multi-accounting, bonus abuse, or chargeback risk, and escalate flagged accounts through the correct channel.

  • Support KYC/AML checks and basic verification steps in line with compliance procedures.

  • Escalate complex, sensitive, or unresolved cases to the correct point of contact (POC) or Slack channel

  • Maintain accurate, complete case notes and interaction logs in the ticketing system for audit and handover purposes.

  • Stay current on new products, promotions, poker formats, and crypto market conditions that affect player questions (e.g., network congestion, gas fees, new coin listings).

  • Identify and report recurring issues, bugs, or player feedback trends to the Team Leader to support continuous improvement.

  • Support responsible gambling protocols, recognising at-risk behaviour and following intervention procedures.

Highly Desired Knowledge and Experience:

  • Excellent written communication in English; clear, empathetic, and concise under pressure.

  • Basic to working knowledge of cryptocurrency: wallets, blockchain confirmations, network fees, common coins (BTC, ETH, USDT, etc.), and how deposits/withdrawals move on-chain.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, 24/7 shift environment, including weekends/holidays.

  • Prior experience in customer support, ideally in iGaming, fintech, or crypto; poker/casino product familiarity is a plus.

  • Strong problem-solving instincts and a proactive, ownership-driven attitude.

  • Familiarity with helpdesk/ticketing tools (e.g., Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk) and Slack-based internal communication.

  • Discretion and judgement when handling financial disputes, fraud flags, and responsible-gambling conversations.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary and performance-based bonuses.

  • Opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in the blockchain and online gaming industry.

  • Flexible working hours and the ability to work fully remotely.

  • A collaborative and inclusive team culture.

  • Professional development opportunities and career growth within a rapidly evolving company.

In this fast-growing company, you will find ample room for growth and innovation alongside the Alignment Health community. Working at Alignment Health provides an opportunity to do work that really matters, not only changing lives but saving them. Together.

The Assistant Vice President, Medicare Risk Adjustment Performance provides executive leadership for Alignment's enterprise Risk Adjustment performance strategy and operations. The role is accountable for achieving annual RAF performance objectives, driving provider and market execution, and ensuring Risk Adjustment activities support the organization's financial, operational, and strategic objectives.

The AVP leads the development and execution of enterprise prospective, concurrent, and retrospective Risk Adjustment strategies and serves as the executive responsible for operational performance across provider engagement, coding operations, chart retrieval, submission, analytics, vendor management, and revenue realization.

The role partners closely with Market Operations, Network Management, Clinical Operations, Finance, Compliance, and Data & Technology teams to ensure enterprise Risk Adjustment goals are achieved while supporting audit readiness, provider performance improvement, and long-term organizational growth.

Enterprise Accountability

  • Accountable for enterprise RAF performance outcomes and annual Risk Adjustment targets.
  • Responsible for prospective, concurrent, and retrospective Risk Adjustment execution strategies.
  • Provides executive oversight for chart retrieval, coding production, provider engagement, and coding submission performance.
  • Establishes market and provider performance objectives and monitors achievement of operational results.
  • Provides executive reporting and recommendations to senior leadership regarding Risk Adjustment performance, opportunities, risks, and resource needs.
  • Oversees strategic vendor partnerships supporting enterprise Risk Adjustment capabilities.

General Duties/Responsibilities (May include but are not limited to):

  • Lead the annual operating plan for Medicare risk adjustment performance, including goals, measures, milestones, resources and market-level execution plans.
  • Provide leadership across prospective, concurrent and retrospective programs, including annual wellness visit support, suspecting and recapture initiatives, chart retrieval, coding production and submission readiness.
  • Establish and monitor performance guidelines for quality, productivity, service levels and financial outcomes; ensure timely executive reporting and action-oriented performance reviews.
  • Use risk adjustment analytics, reporting and strategic business analysis to identify opportunities, risks, root causes and interventions across markets, provider groups and programs.

Finance

  • Accountable for partnership with Finance and Actuarial teams to forecast RAF performance, evaluate revenue implications, monitor financial outcomes, and improve forecast accuracy across markets and programs.
  • Support bid development, revenue forecasting, and long-range planning activities.
  • Evaluate financial impact of provider performance, coding initiatives, and operational investments.
  • Provide executive visibility into Risk Adjustment financial performance and variances.

Vendor Ownership

  • Establish strategic direction and performance expectations for Risk Adjustment vendors and external partners.
  • Oversee vendor contracts, service delivery, productivity, quality, compliance, and business outcomes.
  • Ensure vendor capabilities align with enterprise Risk Adjustment strategy and future-state operating models.

Provider Relationships

  • Serve as executive sponsor for provider coding performance and documentation improvement initiatives.
  • Partner with Network Management, Market Operations and provider leadership to improve enterprise Risk Adjustment outcomes.
  • Lead provider performance reviews, corrective action planning, and performance improvement initiatives across delegated and non-delegated arrangements.
  • Establish accountability frameworks for IPA, provider and vendor performance.
  • Develop scalable reporting, analytical and operational capabilities that improve organizational visibility, support audit readiness and reduce reliance on manual controls.

Data & Technology Strategy

  • Partner with DTS and enterprise analytics teams on Risk Adjustment data strategy and reporting capabilities.
  • Define business requirements supporting workflow modernization, automation, provider enablement, and enterprise reporting.
  • Sponsor technology initiatives that improve scalability, productivity, transparency, and audit readiness.
  • Drive adoption of modern analytics capabilities supporting provider and market performance management.

Revenue Integrity & RADV Readiness Support

  • Ensure chart retrieval, coding production, provider engagement, and submission activities support enterprise RADV readiness objectives.
  • Partner with the AVP, Risk Adjustment Integrity & Transformation on validation findings, reconciliation activities, diagnosis corrections, and audit remediation initiatives.
  • Establish operational accountability for issues impacting diagnosis accuracy, documentation support, evidence availability, and revenue sustainability.
  • Support development of the enterprise MRA business case and modernization initiatives supporting long-term Risk Adjustment performance and audit readiness.
  • Establish policies, procedures, standard work and governance routines that support accurate and compliant execution across products and markets.
  • Maintain knowledge of CMS risk adjustment requirements, model changes and regulatory guidance, and translate changes into operational plans, training and performance expectations.
  • Communicate complex operational, technical and financial information as clear executive insights, decisions and business narratives.
  • Build, mentor and retain a high-performing multidisciplinary team and foster cross-functional accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Strategy & Business Planning

  • Develop multi-year Risk Adjustment performance strategies aligned with enterprise growth objectives.
  • Establish annual goals, objectives, key performance indicators, and resource requirements.
  • Lead business case development for Risk Adjustment investments, operational initiatives, and technology capabilities.
  • Partner with executive leadership on future-state operating model decisions.
  • Support enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning processes.

Primary Control Points and Outcomes

  • Provider workflow enablement: actionable information reaches providers and market teams in time to support appropriate documentation and intervention.
  • Diagnosis capture: eligible opportunities are addressed through compliant prospective, concurrent and retrospective programs.
  • Coding and submission: diagnoses are coded accurately, processed efficiently and submitted through controlled workflows.
  • Performance intelligence: leaders have timely, consistent and decision-ready views of RAF, coding, provider, vendor and market performance.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

Oversees assigned leaders and staff. Responsibilities include workforce planning, recruiting, selecting, orienting and training employees; assigning work; setting goals; monitoring and appraising results; coaching and developing talent; and addressing performance in accordance with company policy.

Minimum Requirements:

Ten or more years of progressive experience in managed care, Medicare Advantage, healthcare analytics, healthcare finance, risk adjustment, population health or related operations.

Experience leading enterprise Risk Adjustment programs across multiple markets and provider arrangements.

Demonstrated responsibility for financial performance, forecasting, strategic planning, or major business initiatives.

Proven track record managing executive stakeholders and enterprise-wide programs.

Education/Licensure:

Other:

Demonstrated knowledge of CMS-HCC risk adjustment methodology, Medicare Advantage reimbursement, coding and documentation programs, encounter data, and performance measurement.

Demonstrated experience designing or leading analytics, reporting, data governance or scalable data infrastructure that supports reporting accuracy, regulatory compliance and audit readiness.

Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives and working with executives, providers, vendors, compliance partners and technical teams.

We are seeking a seasoned Microservices Architect to lead the design and evolution of large-scale microservices ecosystems built on modern container platforms and cloud-native technology stacks. The role requires deep expertise in service decomposition, domain-driven design, distributed data management, and runtime concerns such as resilience, observability, and security at scale. The ideal candidate brings hands-on architectural leadership across complex transformations, with a clear point of view on when microservices are the right answer, how to evolve them safely, and how to keep the resulting estate maintainable over the long term.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Define microservices architecture standards, service boundaries, and decomposition strategies aligned with domain-driven design principles.

  • Design service communication patterns leveraging REST, gRPC, asynchronous messaging, and event streaming as appropriate. Establish API contracts, schema governance, and versioning strategies that enable safe evolution of services over time.
  • Architect resilient distributed systems incorporating circuit breakers, retries, bulkheads, and graceful degradation patterns.
  • Define data ownership models, transactional boundaries, and patterns such as outbox, saga, and CQRS where appropriate.
  • Lead the design of platform capabilities including service mesh, API gateway, identity propagation, and shared observability.

  • Public speaking, open-source contributions, or published technical writing.
  • Experience in regulated industries with strict compliance requirements.

We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer – Big Data & Real-Time Ingestion to join a new project focused on the modernization of a large-scale data platform. The project involves migrating an existing Data Lake and Data Warehouse to a modern architecture designed around real-time data ingestion and streaming. You will contribute to building scalable data pipelines, processing high volumes of data, and enabling real-time analytics within a modern Big Data ecosystem.

What you'll do:

  • Designing and implementing real-time and batch data ingestion pipelines

  • Designing solutions that support low-latency data ingestion and real-time analytics

  • Collaborating with Data Engineers, Architects, and other technical stakeholders to define and implement the target architecture
  • Contributing to technical decisions and the evolution of a modern, real-time data ecosystem

What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years of experience in Data Engineering, preferably working with large-scale data platforms
  • Strong hands-on experience with data ingestion, data pipelines, and distributed data processing
  • Solid experience with real-time data streaming and event-driven architectures
  • Strong understanding of Data Lake and Data Warehouse architectures
  • Hands-on experience with Apache Flink or similar stream-processing technologies
  • Experience with Apache Iceberg or other modern data lakehouse technologies
  • Good understanding of data modelling, data quality, performance optimization, and scalable data architectures
  • Experience working with cloud and/or distributed environments
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills

Nice to have:
